newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Most wool prices improve significantly at NZ sale.
newsitem.headline: Most wool prices improve significantly at NZ sale.

text.p: Prices for most categories of wool improved significantly at the sale in Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The market indicator rose 11 cents to NZ$4.70. The fine segment indicator fell three cents to $8.02, medium segment rose 22 to $5.05, and the strong segment rose 11 cents to $4.36.

Merino fleece 17/18 micron was generally 2.5 to 5.0 percent cheaper but 19 to 22 micron were up to 2.0 percent dearer, while 23 micron was generally 5.0 percent dearer. Halfbred fleece was generally 2.0 to 4.0 percent dearer.

Crossbred fleece 31 to 35 micron was 2.0 to 3.0 percent dearer, while 36 micron and stronger was up to 1.0 percent dearer. Second shear was 1.0-2.0 percent dearer. Bulky skirtings and second shear bellies and pieces were up to 2.0 percent dearer, while crutchings were generally 7.0 percent dearer.
Main interest came from China and Western Europe, with support from local mills, Japan, Turkey, Iran and India. Some 13 percent of the 2,043 tonnes on offer was passed in.

The sale comprised 17 percent crossbred fleece, 33 percent merino, 17 percent halfbred fleece, 10 percent second shear, 8 percent bulky skirtings and miscellaneous other wools. The next sale will be in Napier on October 23 and at Dunedin on October 24.
